title: Career roadmap · Research Assistant
summary: A practical roadmap for entering biological research through laboratory skills, research methodology, molecular biology, experimental design, scientific writing, data analysis, and research-project experience.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a 3-year B.Sc route from 2026–2029, with an optional 4-year honours/research pathway where offered. A research-focused master's degree is a strong next step for progressing beyond entry-level research support.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build cell biology, genetics, microbiology, biochemistry, molecular biology, laboratory methods, statistics, scientific writing, and research methodology.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Complete a relevant master's and gain research-project experience in molecular biology, biotechnology, microbiology, genetics, ecology, neuroscience, biomedical science, or another life-science field.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress toward Senior Research Assistant, Research Associate, Project Associate, Research Scientist-track roles, or specialised laboratory positions.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine biological research with genomics, bioinformatics, automation, AI-assisted analysis, advanced imaging, high-throughput experimentation, and reproducible research.

blocks.text: Complete the first six milestones across six semesters and use semester breaks for laboratory internships or research projects.
Specialisation options

rows.text: Culture + microscopy + microbial genetics + aseptic technique

blocks.text: Evolve and stay relevant · 2035–2046

Research environments are increasingly data-intensive. Develop strong experimental skills first, then add bioinformatics, statistics, scientific programming, image analysis, laboratory automation and reproducible research practices. The ability to work across wet-lab and computational workflows can significantly broaden research opportunities.

2040–2046 relevance

Research assistants who develop into senior scientists will increasingly need to work across wet-lab and computational environments. Genomics, single-cell technologies, advanced imaging, automated experimentation, bioinformatics, AI-assisted literature analysis and reproducible research will increasingly influence biological research.
